chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Remain in a state of purity after you have prayed Fajr, then stand; if you wish, stand near the mountain, and if you wish, stand wherever you wish.
So when you stand, praise Allah, laud Him, and mention from His blessings and trials as much as you are able, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

And let your words be: 'O Allah, Lord of the Sacred Monument, free my neck from the Fire, and expand for me from Your permissible sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the deviant Jinns and humans.'

O Allah, You are the best of those sought, the best of those supplicated to, and the best of those pleaded to. And for every visitor there is a recompense, so make my recompense in this place of mine that You excuse my stumbles, accept my excuses, and overlook my mistakes, then make piety from the world my provision.
Then depart when it brightens for you sufficiently to see the places of the hooves of the camels.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and etiquette for the night of Muzdalifa in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the specific Sunnah of maintaining ritual purity (taharah) after Fajr prayer while stationed at Muzdalifa, emphasizing a prolonged period of dhikr and supplication before the departure to Mina. The prescribed du'a highlights key theological concerns such as deliverance from Hellfire, provision of halal sustenance, and protection from the evil of Jinns and humans, reflecting the Shia emphasis on spiritual preparation during the Hajj rites. The instruction to wait until 'Thabir' (a specific stage of dawn) to depart underscores the precise timing of the Hajj rituals as preserved in Imami tradition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, and Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Become upon the cleanliness after having Prayed Al-Fajr, so you can pause near the mountain if you so desire to, and if you so desire to wherever you want.

So, when you pause, Praise Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and Laud upon Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and mention His<sup>azwj</sup> Favours and His<sup>azwj</sup> Trials as much as you are able to, and send Blessings upon the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and let your words become, ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Sacred Monuments! Free my neck from the Fire, and Expand upon me from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Permissible sustenance, and Turn around from me the evil of the Jinns and the humans. 
O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!

You<sup>azwj</sup> are the best of the sought to, and the best of the supplicated to, and the Best One<sup>azwj</sup> to Plead to. And for every delegate is a Recompense, therefore Make my Recompense to be in this place of mine that You<sup>azwj</sup> should Ignore my stumbles, and Accept my excuses, and Overlook my mistakes, then Make abstention from the world to be my provision’.
Then depart when it brightens for you sufficiently to be able to see the places of the hooves of the camels’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya and ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
you must remain with a valid Wudu’ in the morning. After performing the morning salat (prayer), stay if you like, near the hill, or wherever you like.

Praise Allah and thank Him, speak of His bounties and of His trials as much as you can and say, ‘O Allah, grant salawat (favors and compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause).

This should be of what you may say, ‘O Allah, Lord of al-Mash‘ar al-Haram, set my neck free from hellfire, increase my sustenance of the lawful kind, keep away from me wickedness of sinful Jinn and man.

O Allah, You are the best of those who are sought, the best of those before whom appeals are made and the best of those who are asked for help. Every delegate receives a gift. As gifts for me, ignore my mistakes, accept my excuses and forgive my transgressions; thereafter make piety my supplies of this world.’
Then leave as soon as it becomes bright enough to see the footprints of camels.’”
